method_note: Independent measurement by rater B (rater A's files were never opened). All coordinates are original-image pixels (x right, y down). Landmarks were read from grid-labelled zooms (tools/photo/grid.py plus a private contrast-enhanced grid helper; the enhancement was used only to locate edges, coordinates are always original-pixel labels). Where a structure is hidden by a folded fin, shadow, spray or background clutter the point is null or explicitly flagged as interpolated in notes. For right-facing fish (p031, p038) 'anterior' = larger x, so eye_anterior has the larger x and *_origin is the end of a fin base nearer the head.

photos.orientation_note: Head to the left, left flank toward the camera. Almost pure lateral view (axis rises about 1.8 degrees toward the tail, snout y=279 vs caudal base y=260); dorsal and ventral surfaces are not visible, so roll and pitch are small. Underwater shot through water: low contrast, slight haze, and a pale belly that merges with the stones.
photos.body_curvature_note: Essentially straight. Midline arc length vs straight snout-caudal_base distance is within about 1 percent. Head is held slightly lower than the tail (about 1.8 degrees). Mouth is slightly open (lower jaw dropped).
photos.confidence_reason: Best of the three: sharp head, clean lateral posture, straight body, 9 clearly countable parr marks, eye/pupil and mouth line resolvable at 6-8x zoom. Per-landmark uncertainty: snout +-2 px; eye +-2 px; opercle_post +-5 px (the rear edge is only visible as a faint arc below eye height; at eye height it blends into the red flank); caudal_base +-6 px (taken between the dorsal notch at x about 645 and the ventral fin origin at x about 640, plus the bright crease at x 622-648); dorsal contour +-2 px; ventral contour +-3 px except where the pectoral, pelvic and anal fins lie against the belly (interpolated, +-6 px); anal fin points +-8 px; caudal fork +-8 px (rear fin margin is partly lost against dark water and orange stones).
photos.notes: Species: lateral pattern of 9 grey-blue parr marks with an interspersed row of small round spots below, pink-red lateral band, no red/orange spots, no white fin edges, so consistent with yamame parr (host page is a Yamame species page). Parr marks 1-5 (x 256-515) are tall dark ovals reaching from below the pink stripe to about y 300 (marks 2 and 3 to 307); marks 6-9 (x 547-655) are smaller, fainter and sit higher (y 242-270) on the peduncle. Marks 1-5 also have a fainter bluish upward extension above the pink stripe (y about 245-265) that is not included in top_y. A faint bluish vertical band at x about 300-320, y 225-258 (between marks 1 and 2) is too weak to call a parr mark; the round spot at (298,312) lies below it. Four round dark spots between/below parr marks are listed separately (small_round_spots_between_parr_marks) and are NOT in parr_marks. Measured SL (straight) about 603 px; HL about 175 px (HL/SL about 0.29); eye diameter about 37 px; body depth max about 145 px at x 300-340 (vertical, axis nearly horizontal); peduncle min depth about 52 px at x about 628. Dorsal fin is folded back and leaning (base x 375-466, tip at (457,173)); adipose fin is low and small (about 12 px high, may be partly folded); pectoral fin lies flat against the belly seen almost edge-on (its base points are the dark axil smudge at (213-237, 329-337)); pelvic fin is the yellow triangle x 424-487, y 321-347 hugging the belly (origin = its front attachment, partly hidden); anal fin is a yellow translucent triangle hanging below a sloping belly (x 515-592, y 290-321; origin/end inferred from fin colour boundary, low precision); caudal fin spreads over x 650-770, upper tip at (770,197), lower tip about (750,319). Watermark text lower right (Masahiro Suzuki).

photos.orientation_note: Head to the right, right flank toward the camera, fish airborne and leaving the water. Body axis from snout (924,203) to caudal base (291,258) is tilted about 5 degrees (tail lower), but the tail half bends further downward: the peduncle axis is about 20-25 degrees below the mid-body axis. A thin pale-blue dorsal band along the back (y about 140-150) and a dark ventral band (y about 296-312) are both visible, so roll is modest (about 10-15 degrees). Fins are spread in an unnatural jump posture.
photos.body_curvature_note: Moderate downward arch of the tail (caudal peduncle drops about 55 px relative to the mid-body axis over the last 300 px). Curved SL (midline arc) will exceed straight snout-caudal_base distance by roughly 1-2 percent; the real geometric bend is better seen in the outlines. Pectoral and pelvic fins are deflected down and the caudal fin is crumpled, so fin positions are posture-dependent.
photos.confidence_reason: Geometry of head, trunk and fin bases is measurable, but (1) species identity is doubtful: very dense black spotting including on the dorsal fin rays and above/below the lateral line, a broad pink-rose lateral band, red lower caudal lobe and a very deep body (depth/SL about 0.26) are not typical of yamame; the catalog rates species as unclear (0.4) and the head/jaw rendering looks unusual (maxilla visible only as a pale blade ending under mid-eye); (2) the fish is airborne with a bent tail and splayed, crumpled caudal fin (fork not measurable, ventral outline at pectoral and anal fin zones interpolated); (3) parr marks are not individually resolvable. Recommended: exclude from yamame reference statistics, use only as a qualitative reference.

photos.notes: Measured straight SL about 635 px, HL about 154 px (HL/SL about 0.24), eye diameter about 27 px (eyeball) incl. a pale anterior adipose lid ring from x 838; pupil about 12 px. Max body depth about 165 px near x 640 (vertical chord), i.e. depth/SL about 0.26; peduncle min depth about 50 px (perpendicular) at x 303-324. Opercle_post is taken at the rear edge of the orange gill cover (x about 767-772) rather than the outer edge of the dark cleft behind it (x about 757 in the catalog). Maxilla/mouth: only the pale blade ending at (850,222) is clearly visible; the mouth is closed. Parr marks: faint scale-textured flank; luminance dips averaged over three vertical bands repeat at x about 372, 418, 458, 496, 540, 573, 612, 651, 683, 718, 755 (roughly 38-40 px spacing), which suggests about 10-11 very faint bars, but their top/bottom edges are not visible, so they are listed only as candidate x positions and not as parr_marks. Dorsal fin: dark brown fan with spots, swept back; origin (front of base) at (580,142), rear base (494,167), first-ray apex (502,113) is the highest point; fin base line is straight, so the body outline in x 494-580 follows it. Adipose fin: brown rounded lobe x 321-354, y 187-215, base on the sloping back. Pectoral fin: orange blade hanging vertically from the axil (base spans x 766-790 at y about 257, tip about (762,329)); the two base points are the posterior and anterior ends of the horizontal base line because the fin is rotated, not true dorsal/ventral ends. Pelvic fin (orange) hangs from (572,306) to tip about (534,362). Anal fin: large translucent brown-red fan x 330-433, base along the sloping belly, longest ray tip about (345,327), partly overlapped by spray. Caudal fin: upper lobe tip (241,203), lower red lobe tip about (246,319); trailing edge nearly straight x 243-253 and broken by spray, so no fork recorded; a small flag-like flap at (242-270, 266-273).

photos.orientation_note: Small fish (SL about 205 px, head only about 54 px) lying on a wet rock, photographed from above; head at lower right, right flank up toward the camera. Axis is tilted about 16 degrees (tail up-left). A dark dorsal band is visible along the upper edge, so the back is rolled toward the camera by about 15-20 degrees. Heavily over-exposed and JPEG-compressed, so the flank is nearly white and edges are soft.
photos.body_curvature_note: Body is straight (midline arc within 1 percent of the straight snout-caudal_base distance). The caudal fin is bent up-left and partly overlaps a dark crack. The roll of the dorsal surface slightly exaggerates apparent depth of the dorsal outline.
photos.confidence_reason: Usable for parr-mark number, spacing and rough proportions, but the fish is tiny (1 px = 0.5 percent of SL), over-exposed and blurred; the head is obscured by a hook line/leader and a gaping mouth, the snout tip at x 430 is uncertain by +-4 px (a thin line continues to x about 440), mouth/maxilla points are not resolvable, dorsal, pectoral, anal and caudal fins are only partly visible, and the dorsal surface is rolled toward the camera. Parr mark heights are +-3 px. Species is also uncertain because of three orange spots (see notes).
photos.notes: Nine blue-grey parr marks (x 246-370) of increasing size from the head backwards then decreasing: the first mark (x 246) lies just in front of the caudal base and the last (x 370) just behind the gill cover; marks 5-6 (x 306, 322) are the tallest (14-16 px, soft upper edge, core about 7-8 px) and the marks lean about 15 degrees with the body axis. Mark heights listed include the soft upper edge (R-channel below about 175); core heights are 6-10 px. Three small orange-pink spots lie between parr marks 6-7, 7-8 and 8-9 at about (331,236), (348,243), (363,247) on the lateral-line height; in an over-exposed photo these may be amago-type red spots or pale artefact, so species yamame vs amago cannot be settled from this photo. The head: eye pupil about 5.5 px, pale gold ring about 13-14 px, eye centre (404.5,264.5); snout tip estimated at (430,273) but jaws look protruding/open (dead or hooked fish), so snout length (snout to eye_anterior about 18 px, 0.34 HL) is probably over-estimated; HL about 54 px (HL/SL about 0.26). Fin notes (all low precision): dorsal fin lies folded back on the dorsal surface with striated rays at x 318-336, y 196-216 (origin = front of base at about (336,215), tip about (322,196)); pectoral fin is a grey strip lying along the belly edge, x 346-374, y 257-270 (base at the gill cover); a peach-orange sliver at x 256-282, y 241-250 just below the belly line is taken as the anal fin (front end (281,243), tip (257,246)); the pelvic fin and the adipose fin were not seen. Caudal fin: brown-orange, upper lobe toward (210,190), lower lobe toward (206,237), fork unclear. Measured straight SL about 204 px; max body depth about 43 px perpendicular (0.21 SL) near x 315-327; peduncle min depth about 17.5 px (0.086 SL) at x 244-246.
